LESSON: FRACTIONS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.6: Fractions

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Fractions. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: When can you usefractions in real life? 2. 2. How can yourepresent fractions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the numerator and denominator in a fraction in different situations,
2. represent a fraction with denominators not exceeding 12 as part of a whole and as part of a group,
3. identify different types of fractions in real-life situations,
4. convert improper fractions to mixed fractions in different situations, e) convert mixed numbers to improper fractions in different contexts, f) appreciate application of fractions in real-life situations. SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Fractions.
2. Explain Fractions to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: discuss the top (numerator) and bottom (denominator) numbers in a fraction and share with others,
4. Show that you can: identify the numerator and denominator in a fraction in different situations,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Fractions. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: When can you usefractions in real life? 2. 2. How can yourepresent fractions?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss the top (numerator) and bottom (denominator) numbers in a fraction and share with others,
2. Illustrate, in pairs/groups, fractions as part of a whole or part of a group using cut- outs, counters or clock face,
3. Work out, in groups, proper, improper and mixed fractions as part of a whole or as part of a group using paper cut-outs or counters,

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. identify the numerator and denominator in a fraction in different situations,
2. represent a fraction with denominators not exceeding 12 as part of a whole and as part of a group,
3. identify different types of fractions in real-life situations,
4. convert improper fractions to mixed fractions in different situations, e) convert mixed numbers to improper fractions in different contexts, f) appreciate application of fractions in real-life situations.
